hook_text: Same brief, two completely different answers, drawn in ten minutes each on squared paper. Here is the method.
clip_script: Draw a tall trapezium, feint: base line, two legs leaning in, a short top. From the right corners, lines back at 45 degrees, half the depth. Join them: back legs. Darken the four legs. Horizontals at your ticks, diagonals as a zigzag or an X, a little braced platform with antennas on top, a concrete block below. Label it: tube legs for rigidity, X on every face, string inside against twist, webs at the base. That is idea one, a four-legged tapered lattice. Now idea two, and it must be different in structure, not colour. Three legs, so it is a triangle in plan and already stiff. K bracing. Folded channel legs. A weighted base. A canopy of card leaves hiding the antennas. Same scale, side by side, and under each one two honest sentences: what it does well, where it might fail. Feint first, dark after, show the pattern not every member. Two towers, one sheet, ready to be judged.
visual_style: Whiteboard squared grid; a trapezium grows depth and members into a lattice tower, then a three-legged canopy tower appears beside it with notes and leader lines.
mood: Brisk and creative, the design taking shape stroke by stroke.
pacing: Step-by-step build of tower one, fast list of ways to differ, tower two assembled, closing habits.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and sketch both of your tower ideas on one A3 sheet.
